# Plan: SPE round 3

I assume the spec lives at `spe/spec/spec.md` and that round 3 reuses round 2's file layout and hit rule.

## 1. What round 2 taught us

- The naive guess ("same as last round") was closer than my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. The one hit was a tie.
- Every round 2 prediction expected an improvement. None of them came true. My predictions moved too far from the baseline.
- C's Why was wrong. Merging the tools hid the outage status lookup (F4). Outage tickets then got P3.
- F5 changed the grader in round 2. The round 1 priority number (0.78) came from the old grader. So 0.78 is not a fair baseline. Round 3 compares against round 2's regraded numbers only.

## 2. Decisions on the proposals

You asked me to work on my own, so I decide each proposal and record the reason in the spec.

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Accept | F4 has a clear mechanism, and r02-C-T17-1..3 lets us test it. |
| P2 | Accept, with a change | New tickets change the test set. The naive baseline then stops being comparable. I add the 10 tickets as a separate split named `hard-r03`. The 0.86 numbers are reported on the old set only. |
| P3 | Accept | D's cost went up from $0.003 to $0.004 because of F6. I mark F6 as "parked, D dropped" and not as fixed. If D comes back, F6 has to be fixed first. |
| P4 | Accept | B missed by 0.02. That gap is within noise at 3 trials. Five trials per cell gives a tighter estimate. |

## 3. Step 1: Update the spec

Changes to `spe/spec/spec.md`:

1. Rename "Proposed for round 3 (not yet agreed)" to "Round 3 changes (agreed)". Add a Decision column with the text from section 2.
2. Configs for round 3 are A, B, and C. C keeps its other merged tools. Only the outage status check is split out again.
3. Ticket sets are `core` (unchanged from round 2) and `hard-r03` (10 new tickets that mix billing and outage).
4. There are 5 trials per cell.
5. Baselines come from round 2's regraded results only.
6. Add a new prediction rule. Each prediction names the tickets its mechanism touches. The predicted change can be no larger than the share of those tickets in the set.
7. Add a labeling note. I write the labels for `hard-r03` myself. They are unreviewed. Results on that split are marked as provisional until you check the labels.

Update `spe/failures.md`. F4 becomes "fix in r03 (P1)". F6 becomes "parked, D dropped in r03".

**Commit 1 (local only):** `spe: round 3 spec, agree P1-P4`

## 4. Step 2: The prediction (round 3)

The file is `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It replaces `r03-draft.yaml`, and its status is `frozen`. I remove D from `baseline_same_as_last_round` because D is dropped. I add the priority and cost baselines from round 2's regraded results files. The draft is missing both.

Before freezing, I count the outage tickets in `core`. That count sets the ceiling for C's priority gain.

| Metric | Config | Set | Naive (r02) | Predicted | Why | What would prove the Why wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | core | 0.86 | 0.86 | A did not change. It is the control. | A moves by more than 0.03. That would point to drift in the model or the grader. |
| category accuracy | B | core | 0.86 | 0.86 | B did not change. Round 2's miss was noise. | B is under 0.83 or over 0.89 with 5 trials. |
| category accuracy | C | core | 0.80 | 0.82 | The split restores the status lookup. Some outage tickets get the correct category again. Other merged tools stay, so the recovery is only partial. | C is still 0.80 or lower. Or C goes back up while the T17 traces still show no status call. |
| priority accuracy | C | core | 0.71 | 0.76, capped at the outage-ticket share | C calls the status check again, so outage tickets get P1 or P2 instead of P3. | The T17 trials still skip the status check, or the outage tickets still get P3. |
| cost per ticket | C | core | r02 C value | r02 C value plus at most 10% | Outage tickets now make one extra tool call. | Cost rises by more than 10%. That would mean the split adds retries or loops. |
| category accuracy | A, B, C | hard-r03 | 0.86 (core value used as the naive guess) | 0.70 | Mixed tickets have two plausible categories. | Accuracy is above 0.80, which means the set is not harder. Or it is below 0.55, which means the labels are probably wrong. |

The hit rule stays the same as round 2. The "Closer" column is still scored against the naive guess.

**Commit 2 (local only):** `spe: freeze round 3 predictions`

I commit the predictions before any eval runs. That way nobody can change them after seeing the results.

## 5. Step 3: The dynamic workflow for round 3

The script is `spe/evals/r03/workflow.js`, and this plan is saved as `spe/plans/r03-plan.md`. Orchestrator subagents use Opus. The configs under test keep their own models.

**Phase 0. Preflight (one agent, blocks everything else)**
- Check that the git tree is clean and that commit 2 exists.
- Check that `grade.py` reads `label.priority` (F5). Run it on 3 stored round 2 transcripts. Confirm that it reproduces the regraded round 2 scores.
- Check that config C exposes the outage status check as its own tool.
- Check that `hard-r03` has 10 tickets, each with both labels. If any check fails, the workflow stops and writes the reason to `spe/evals/r03/preflight.md`.

**Phase 1. Run the cells (fans out in parallel)**
- 3 configs × 2 sets × 5 trials gives 30 cells. Each cell is one agent task.
- An agent retries a cell only for infrastructure errors such as timeouts or rate limits. It never retries a cell because of a bad answer.
- Each agent writes its raw transcripts to `spe/evals/r03/runs/<config>-<set>-<trial>/`.

**Phase 2. Grade (fans out per cell)**
- Run `grade.py` on every cell. Collect accuracy, priority, and cost into `spe/evals/r03/results.csv`.

**Phase 3. Branches that depend on the results**
- If C's priority is under 0.76, an agent reads the C outage traces, starting with T17. It reports whether the status check was called. This tests the Why, not only the number.
- If any config scores below 0.55 on `hard-r03`, an agent reviews those labels and flags any that look wrong. It does not change grades.
- If A moves by more than 0.03, an agent checks for grader or model drift before any other conclusion is drawn.
- No branch adds trials after the results are seen.

**Phase 4. Write up (one agent)**
- Add the round 3 section to `spe/prediction-log.md` with the same columns as round 2.
- Add one line that names which Why broke, or that says none broke.
- Add any new failures to `spe/failures.md` as F7 and later.
- Add "Proposed for round 4 (not yet agreed)" to the spec.

**Commit 3 (local only), after the workflow is built and before it runs:** `spe: round 3 eval workflow`

**Commit 4 (local only), after the results are written:** `spe: round 3 results and log`

No commit is pushed. No commit message mentions Claude.

- The `hard-r03` labels are mine and nobody has reviewed them. Its numbers stay provisional until you check them.
- With D gone, F6 is untested. The retry bug may also affect A, B, or C on long tickets. Phase 4 reports token counts per ticket length so we can see it.
- Five trials costs about 67% more than three. Without D the total is lower. If round 2 cost reports exist, I give an estimate from them before Phase 1 runs.
